revision: F16 recount (2026-09-13), following monogate 6890c967: every core entry is counted in the sixteen operators on monogate.org/framework, and each construction is evaluated numerically on its domain by the monogate repository's python/tests/test_superbest_f16_constructions.py. The positive headline and the general basket follow python/monogate/superbest.py's SUPERBEST_F16_POS_* and SUPERBEST_F16_GEN_*; the count with ln x = EXL(0, x) as one node is kept as totals.total_positive_with_exl (SUPERBEST_V53_POS_*).
breakthrough: add_gen = 2n discovered via LEdiv+DEML construction: lediv(x, deml(y,1)) = ln(exp(x)/exp(-y)) = x+y for ALL real x,y
X20_finding: EPL(x,y) = exp(x*ln(y)) = y^x is one of the 16 F16 operators (ELMl in Sixteen_Operator_Census). Therefore pow(x,y) = x^y = EPL(y,x) for x>0 is a single 1-node F16 application — not 3n. The 3n construction was for general domain where x can be negative (ln(x) undefined). This resolves the F17d paradox in X20.

construction_detail.combined: LEDIV(x, DEML(y,1)) = ln(exp(x)/exp(-y)) = ln(exp(x)*exp(y)) = ln(exp(x+y)) = x+y

completeness: Every one of the ten operations has an F16 construction on the positive domain. Over all reals exp, neg, add, sub, mul, recip (x != 0) and div (y != 0) each have one tree; ln, sqrt and pow have no all-reals entry, and no real F16 tree computes abs. Entries are best-known upper bounds; none is shown minimal.

open_problem_resolved.now: add_gen <= 2n by the explicit construction LEdiv(x, DEML(y,1)). The 11n construction was not optimal.
open_problem_resolved.implication: Every polynomial-like sum of signed terms drops from 11n to 2n per addition.

X20_resolution.paradox: F17d in X20 asked: if ELMl is in the 16-operator census, why is pow = 3n?
X20_resolution.resolution: ELMl = EPL(x,y) = exp(x*ln(y)) = y^x IS in F16. pow(x,n) = x^n = EPL(n,x) for x>0 is 1 node. The 3n construction (EXL+ELAd+EML) was an expanded decomposition that failed to recognize EPL as a usable primitive. For positive domain: pow = 1n. The general-domain 3n was the expanded-tree path on x > 0; since the F16 recount of 2026-09-13 the table has no all-reals pow entry.
X20_resolution.downstream_note: Any catalog equations containing pow(x,n) with positive base x have their positive-domain cost reduced by 2 nodes per pow occurrence.

linear_cost_law_update.note: The positive/general distinction collapses for add/sub/neg. mul and pow retain domain splits.
